title: At-least-once: a crash before the ack means the message comes back
caption: The broker can't tell 'crashed before the work' from 'crashed after it', so it redelivers. Only an idempotent consumer makes the duplicate harmless.

messages.label: deliver m7 (charge order 42)
messages.note: The broker hides m7 from other consumers for a visibility timeout, say 30 s.

messages.label: crash before ack
messages.note: The work is done, but the ack never reaches the broker.

messages.label: redeliver m7
messages.note: Same message, same id, second delivery.

messages.label: INSERT, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
messages.note: msg_id is the unique key, which turns the second charge into a no-op.

messages.label: ack m7
messages.note: Now the broker deletes it. One message, two deliveries, one effect.

scenarios.name: Plain INSERT: charged twice
scenarios.summary: Same crash, but the consumer isn't idempotent: the redelivered message charges order 42 a second time.

messages.label: crash before ack
messages.note: The broker never hears that m7 is done.

messages.label: redeliver m7
messages.note: After the visibility timeout, m7 goes to another consumer.

messages.label: INSERT payment for order 42
messages.note: No unique key on msg_id, so a second row is written: the customer pays twice.

scenarios.name: Alternative: ack first
scenarios.summary: At-most-once: ack before doing the work. No duplicates ever, but a crash in between loses the message for good.

messages.label: ack m7
messages.note: The consumer acks as soon as it receives. The broker deletes m7.

messages.label: INSERT payment for order 42
messages.note: This write never happens, and the broker has nothing left to redeliver. Fine for metrics, not for payments.

scenarios.name: Handler outlives timeout
scenarios.summary: No crash at all: a handler slower than the visibility timeout gets its message redelivered while it's still working. Size the timeout above p99, or extend it while working.

messages.label: slow INSERT (45 s)
messages.note: The database is under load. Consumer 1 is alive, just slow.

messages.label: redeliver m7 at 30 s
messages.note: The broker can't tell slow from dead, so m7 is visible again and goes to consumer 2.

messages.label: INSERT, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
messages.note: Two consumers work on the same message at once. Only the idempotent write keeps this safe.

messages.label: ack m7 (late)
messages.note: Fix: extend the timeout while working (a heartbeat / ChangeMessageVisibility), or size it above the slowest handler.
